{"subject":"Predictable p99 for a multi-region data layer","body":"Hi Tom,

It looks like the Northwind Payments team is focused on capacity planning and on evaluating cost and latency improvements across its multi-region data layer.

If tail latency is part of that evaluation, this might be relevant: ScyllaDB uses a shard-per-core C++ architecture with no JVM garbage-collection pauses, which is aimed at keeping p99 latency predictable rather than spiky.

Would a short technical write-up on how that architecture handles read latency be useful as you work through the evaluation?

Oz
GTM Engineer, ScyllaDB
